newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers to "remind" Netanyahu of rightist promises.
newsitem.headline: Settlers to "remind" Netanyahu of rightist promises.

text.p: Restive Jewish settler leaders warned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday he must make good on campaign promises to expand settlements or face "reminders" of his vows with a nationwide wave of protests.

"If there be no alternative, we will reach the same level of intensity as before the election (to influence) public opinion," said Nisan Smoliansky, "Operations Chief" of the settler umbrella organisation YESHA.
He told reporters this could mean "gigantic demonstrations, on the hills or in any other place, in order that the prime minister will be reminded of his own policy."

For years settlers spearheaded a campaign of torchlight rallies and highway blockades to unseat the governments of slain Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and his successor Shimon Peres, who paved the way for landmark Israeli-PLO peace deals by freezing most settlement construction in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

YESHA leaders, in an "emergency" meeting, said Netanyahu's government was delaying the resumption of settlement housing construction and a promised go-ahead for some 3,000 settler families to move into already finished homes in the West Bank.

Settlers have viewed with concern the U.S.-prodded resumption this week of Israeli-Palestinian talks toward implementing a long-delayed army withdrawal from much of Hebron, the only West Bank town with a settler population.

Palestinians view the pullout as an acid test of Netanyahu's intentions regarding the fragile peace process, rocked last month by 75 dead in the bloodiest Israeli-Palestinian clashes since self-rule began in 1994.
But settlers oppose a withdrawal, fearing the town's 400 settlers, outnumbered 250 to one by Hebron Palestinians, would be rendered vulnerable to attack.
Israel's main ally Washington has in the past strongly opposed resumption of construction in the settlements, which it has termed a main obstacle to peace.

The 130,000 armed settlers who live among the two million Palestinians of the West Bank and Gaza proved a potent force in Israel's May elections, voting for Netanyahu in large numbers and helping him oust Peres in a come-from-behind upset victory.
